source.title: Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5 ("Local Government Elections: Nominations in Tyrone"); Ulster Herald, 29 April 1939, p. 5 ("Local Government Elections: No contest in Omagh Rural District")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: 'For the following electoral divisions no nominations were received:— ... previous member ...'; 'the returning members are deemed to have been re-elected' (same report)

note: Triennial election of the Omagh rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations closed on Tuesday 18 April 1939. Thirty-five divisions received nominations; the only double nomination, Mullaghslin, ended with Patrick Conway's withdrawal, and 'There will be no contests in Omagh Rural district' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1939, p. 5). In Drumquin, Fintona, Sluggan and Liffer no nominations were received and the previous members are 'deemed to have been re-elected' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5). No party labels are printed in the list. No poll was held; the folder date is the provisional Tyrone polling day. No nomination was received; the paper names the previous member, who was deemed re-elected (recorded as returned unopposed, as the earlier rounds do for no-nomination divisions). Returned unopposed.
